newsitem.title: Tajikistan: Tajik warlord quits centre of disputed town.
newsitem.headline: Tajik warlord quits centre of disputed town.

text.p: Tanks and most troops of the mutinous commander of the Tajik government's elite armoured brigade left the centre of Tursunzade in western Tajikistan on Friday but it was unclear whether the unit had returned to barracks.

Reuters correspondent Chris Bird saw no tanks or other armour and only a handful of troops at the town's centre where the rebel commander, Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev, and his men had been based on Thursday.

Khudoyberdyev, who led an armed rebellion against the government last February, sent his brigade into Tursunzade, an aluminium-producing town 45 km (30 miles) west of the capital Dushanbe, on Wednesday to unseat a local strongman.
Embattled Tajik President Imamali Rakhmonov ordered the commander back to barracks, saying his action was "illegal".

A local official said Khudoyberdyev's forces had left for the southern town of Kurgan-Tyube but rumours circulated in Tursunzade that the commander had hidden his tanks inside a sprawling aluminium plant.
A senior plant official said the smelter was still operating at 40-45 percent of its 500,000 tonnes per year capacity.
Khudoyberdyev promised on Thursday to obey his president and return to barracks near Kurgan-Tyube.
But his decision to send in tanks and armour against the irregular force of a local opponent highlighted the remote, Central Asian republic's slide into armed anarchy.
He also said a small group would remain to "restore order" in the town 45 km (30 miles) west of the capital Dushanbe.

On Wednesday, Rakhmonov threatened to treat his renegade commander as a "war criminal" after Khudoyberdyev moved troops and armour on his own initiative to Tursunzade to rid the town of local strongman Kodir Abdulayev.
The Tajik leader has his hands full already. The former Soviet republic has been torn by a four-year civil war with Islamic guerillas which has left tens of thousands dead.
